boundary_rationale: Onset weighed both sides: Ezek.45.18 carries BOTH a full month+day date formula AND the messenger formula in the same verse -- the exact combination that reads like a fresh oracle onset. On the onset side, the messenger formula (also present at 44.6, 44.9, 45.9, 46.1, 46.16, 47.13 in this part) opens what looks like a new speech; but the date clause carries no year word, so it fails the book's structural dateline test (a YEAR word together with a month or day term) -- it is one of exactly four calendar dates in the book (45.18, 45.20, 45.21, 45.25) that carry a month/day construction without a year, and none of the fourteen year-bearing datelines falls anywhere in this part. On the close side, the preceding row (45.9-17) already closed at the Ezek.45.17 samekh, and the addressee and topic (the cultic calendar under the temple-law section opened at 45.9) do not change at 45.18 -- there is no addressee-class shift of the kind that would corroborate a fresh onset.
